answer: Each agent holds an ivory‑colored hash that links its identity to a proof‑of‑work submitted in the last epoch. At every new epoch the network publishes an umber‑tinted challenge drawn from a meadow of recent transaction snapshots, requiring every identity to compute fresh reasoning to refresh its credential; missing the deadline revokes the identity. Thus an attacker must spend full model compute for each fake node each epoch, making a Sybil attack linearly expensive in GPU cycles.
